summary: Central operations role cannot assume analytics service account: blocked by organization-level conditional role binding
description: Issue summary: Operations central-ops role (redwood-central-ops@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com) is failing when attempting to impersonate the analytics service account used for nightly data ingestion (analytics-ingest@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com). Impact: Scheduled ingestion jobs started failing at 03:10 UTC on 2026-03-12 triggering downstream data freshness alerts for analytics dashboards and model retraining pipelines. Scope: affects prod analytics ingestion in us-central1 and attempts from SRE automation in us-east1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a workstation with gcloud configured as redwood-central-ops, run: gcloud auth login && gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=...
2) Attempt to generate access token: gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=analytics-ingest@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
3) Observe permission denied error referencing org policy condition or deniedAssumeRole
4) Confirm scheduled Cloud Scheduler job logs show 403 when using impersonation path
observed_logs: 2026-03-12T03:11:05Z ERROR cloud-scheduler: http status 403 (PermissionDenied): Caller does not have permission to impersonate service account analytics-ingest@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud: ERROR: (gcloud.auth.print-access-token) PermissionDenied: The caller is not authorized to impersonate the service account.
OrgPolicy audit log: principals/110987654321 had request to iam.serviceAccounts.generateAccessToken denied by ORG_POLICY_CONDITIONAL_BINDING
hypothesis: An organization-level IAM Condition was recently tightened (see confluence page) restricting 'iam.serviceAccountUser' to principals with a specific attribute or tag.
central-ops role does not match that attribute and therefore fails the condition, causing impersonation to be denied even though project-level bindings exist.
Possible regression introduced by infra PR that deployed the org policy change in prod org on 2026-03-11.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Aisha: Initial ticket created after alarms from analytics on-call.
2026-03-12 10:05 UTC - Tomas: Confirmed 403s across 4 scheduler jobs and manual impersonation attempts.
2026-03-12 12:40 UTC - SRE ran gcloud iam roles list and confirmed central-ops has role roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator at project level.

2026-03-12 14:30 UTC - Checked OrgPolicy for constraint 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' and custom conditional bindings. New policy 'restrict-sa-impersonation' found applied at org level on 2026-03-11 by infra-deploy bot.
2026-03-13 08:10 UTC - Pulled audit logs showing rule evaluation: binding evaluated to false for principal attribute 'resource.name.startsWith("projects/serviceAccounts/analytics-")' mismatch.
2026-03-13 11:00 UTC - Reproduced issue in staging by temporarily applying same conditional binding; confirmed identical failure mode.
2026-03-14 06:55 UTC - Reached out to infra owners in #infra-config and created PR to tweak condition to allow central-ops (PR linked).
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Critical - dashboards showing 24-hour lag. Need ETA for workaround.
Tomas Rivera (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Investigating, initial hint points to org-level IAM condition applied 2026-03-11. Will validate policy and audit logs.
SRE Team 2026-03-12: Confirmed manifest of failures across scheduler and manual impersonation. Noted that project-level bindings exist but conditions evaluate to false.
Infra owner (via Slack) 2026-03-13: We rolled out a tighten policy in response to compliance request. We can prepare emergency exception if verified.

Tomas Rivera 2026-03-14: Created https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427 proposing an amended condition and emergency allowlist for redwood-central-ops. Requesting review from infra owners.
mitigation: Short-term workaround: run ingestion jobs using an alternative service account that already meets the org policy attributes (analytics-ingest-legacy@...).

Temporary fix applied: CI created emergency allowlist binding for principal redwood-central-ops in org policy 'restrict-sa-impersonation' — change is staged in infra PR; awaiting approval and manual promotion to prod.
Fallback: re-run failed ingestion jobs manually once the allowlist is in place.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation in progress: emergency allowlist prepared in infra PR #1427 and tested in staging; awaiting infra-owner approval for promotion to production. No permanent resolution until org policy condition is widened or operations role is tagged with required attribute. Documented follow-up items and TO-DOs in next_steps.
next_steps: 1) Get infra owner approval for PR #1427 and schedule a controlled rollout to production during low-traffic window (2026-03-15 02:00 UTC). 2) Update central-ops service identity to include required attribute/tags as alternative permanent fix. 3) Post-change: monitor ingest success rate and close ticket after 48 hours of stable runs. 4) Add a runbook entry describing process to request org-policy exceptions for emergency SRE access.
